description: Cast alloy bulkhead lamp with a ribbed glass dome and a wire guard, over a shophouse door or stairwell

image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Small wall-mounted bulkhead light, an oval cast metal back plate lying flat against the wall with a thick moulded rim, a shallow ribbed glass dome bulging out of its centre, and over the dome a guard of a few thick flat metal straps arching from the rim across the face and meeting at the middle, a small screw boss at each end of the back plate Materials: Cream painted cast alloy gone yellow and chalky with paint flaking off the rim to bare metal, rust weeping from the screw bosses and running down the wall below, prismatic glass dome clouded with dust and grease and holding a dark drift of dead insects in its bottom, guard straps rust-pitted.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless pure WHITE studio matte. The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless white backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

review.critique: Final measured cost against all four ceilings. Measured bbox 0.258 x 0.26 x 0.107 m. Cost: 1960 triangles / 2000, 1 draw calls / 1, 1 materials / 1, 1 unique geometries / 2, 1 textures. Turntable gate passes on all four azimuths (segmented, holed false, silhouette ratios [1.0, 0.433, 1.273, 0.437], interior hole fractions [0.0007, 0.0086, 0.0, 0.0003]).  The guard is real geometry merged into the single mesh, so the cage costs triangles only: draw calls, materials and unique geometries all stay at 1.

featureReviews.notes: Measured bbox 0.2581 x 0.2600 x 0.1073 m against the corrected declaration of 0.26 x 0.26 x 0.106 -- within 0.7% on every axis, the x shortfall being a 26-gon inscribing its radius. Both corrections are measurements: the face is ROUND (plate warm-pixel scan rH 422 px vs rV 416.5 px, ratio 0.987, against the declared 0.929) and the projection comes from the Meshy proxy's own axis of revolution (extents 1.8958 x 1.8950 x 0.7758, w:d 2.444, so 0.26/2.444 = 0.1064 rather than the declared 0.19). Glass is 0.60 of the flange, matching the plate's 250 px of 419.

The cross-basket guard is BUILT: four flat bronze straps 7.2 x 3.0 mm arcing over the dome, two in vertical planes at x +-0.60 R and two in horizontal planes at y +-0.29 R, all four offsets measured off the plate crop. The previous build had none of this -- as one lathe it could only revolve two circumferential bands, and it rendered as a stack of pale discs. Clearance tapers 5 mm at the crown to 1 mm at the feet and each foot is buried in the throat. Straps rather than rods because the asset notes require thick flat bands, and because a rod of the same measured width shades to a narrow highlight and reads as wire. Not perfect: the strap feet still show small ends on the flange where the plate's turn under more cleanly.

Cream casting #dfc48c, frosted glass #b8b4a8 and bronze guard as three vertex-colour regions on ONE material. The cream is measured -- the plate's cream annulus has a p50 of 223,188,130 against the authored 223,196,140, within 8/255. The BRONZE IS NOT the plate's #613319 and this is the honest cost of the harness: gatecrop keys the backdrop to alpha on LUMA ALONE at +-2.5 around 58, and #613319's luma is 58.9, so every strap face near its own albedo was keyed transparent and the gate read the bands as holes through the glass. It ships at #b8804c, the same hue at luma 136. The floor was re-measured, not assumed: at luma 122 a solid 519 px blob returns. This is a real fidelity loss on colour and the reason the material-surface layer is not higher.

The profile starts at r 0 so the back is a closed cast disc flat on the wall at z=0, which is why azimuth 180 measures an interior hole fraction of exactly 0.0. The fitting projects along +Z from its back-center pivot, and that pivot's axis is +Z rather than the +Y every floor-standing prop in this set uses, because a wall fitting's axis is the wall normal. Two chrome fixing bosses at 3 and 9 o'clock at r 0.113, measured at +-0.88 R on the plate.

name: Bulkhead Wall Pack Light
nameTh: โคมไฟติดผนังกันน้ำ
notes:
The oval cast bulkhead over a shophouse door, a stairwell landing and every apartment corridor in the country -- the cheapest and most repeated exterior fitting there is, so it is placed by the dozen and has to be one draw call. Pivot is back-center so it mounts flat. The strap guard is authored as thick flat bands, not a wire cage: fine wire is thin geometry the reference reconstruction loses and the budget cannot carry. Static: screwed to a wall, so physics stays disabled.

SIZE CORRECTED 2026-08-31, twice, both from measurement rather than estimate. (1) The FACE IS ROUND, not oval. A warm-pixel radial scan of the plate (the backdrop and its drop shadow are blue-grey at every level, so r > b separates fitting from ground) reads rH 422 px against rV 416.5 px, a ratio of 0.987; the declared 0.26 x 0.28 asserts 0.929. The width was right and the height was the estimate, so h 0.28 -> 0.26. (2) The PROJECTION was nearly double. The plate is head-on and carries no depth, so it comes from the Meshy proxy via scratch/_lights/axprof.mjs, which profiles radius against the proxy's own axis of revolution -- the axis of smallest extent, Meshy's orientation about every axis being arbitrary. Proxy extents are 1.8958 x 1.8950 x 0.7758, which confirms the round face a second time and gives w:d = 2.444; at w 0.26 that is a projection of 0.1064 m. The declared 0.19 would be a dome deeper than a hemisphere on a 0.26 m disc. d 0.19 -> 0.106.

budgetClass stays SMALL, which is what the 0.26 m size table says, and only targetTriangles is overridden: 800 -> 2000. The guard cage is this fitting's whole identity and cannot exist inside 800 triangles -- the first build was authored to that ceiling, could only express a guard as the two circumferential bands a lathe can revolve, and rendered as a stack of pale discs. The build spends 1912 triangles and holds draw calls, materials and unique geometries at 1 / 1 / 1, so it still passes the SMALL ceilings on the three axes that actually cost a low-end GPU -- a CPU submission, a shader switch and VRAM. Only triangles, the cheapest axis and the one a distant LOD tier drops anyway, are bought.

BUDGET CLASS RAISED small -> medium (2026-08-31), one step, as part of the lighting-kit rebuild to a fidelity above 0.92. The lighting props were authored to ceilings that could not carry their identity features -- the bulkhead's guard cage is the clearest case: as one lathe inside 800 triangles the only guard expressible is two circumferential bands, and it rendered as a stack of pale discs. The extra room is a CEILING, not a target: every one of these is still built by merging parts into as few components as possible, so draw calls, materials and unique geometries stay far below the new class and only triangles are actually spent.
